title: Annotatio III §.XI close: Translocation / Transfiguration, not Transsubstantiation — ask for Vicesubstantiation; stop before Annotatio IV
pass_a_gloss: To what Substance then, or whence its Trans? What Transsubstantiation is here? This is indeed a Translocation; for they will have the Body succeed from Heaven into the Place of the Bread’s Substance; And it is a Transfiguration; for they say the Holy Body submits itself to the Figure which the fugitive Bread had borne in its Species (left behind itself rather unkindly). But what else is it? Therefore the Roman Correctors are to be asked that they now be willing to correct even that Autun ἀκυρολογία, and (if fatal necessity so bears that Error always beget Error to Error, and the Prodigy of Dogma and name be forever marked with a stribiligo) that starting from another little letter they now order this to be called, instead of Transsubstantiation, Vicesubstantiation.
pass_b_english: So where is the Trans? This is translocation (body from heaven into bread’s place) and transfiguration (holy body under the fugitive bread’s leftover figure) — not Transsubstantiation.
Ask the Roman correctors to fix Autun’s misnomer: if error must breed error, start from another letter and call it Vicesubstantiation.
Stop before Annotatio IV (true Eucharistic sentence through the ages).
source_text: Cui igitur Substantia, aut unde suum Trans? Qua heic Transsubstantiatio est? Translocatio quidem ista est; Succedere enim volunt Corpus de Cælo in Locum Substantiæ Panis; Et Transfiguratio est; Submittere enim se aiunt Sanctum Corpus Figuræ, quam profugus Panis in Speciebus suis (satis inclementer post se relictis) gesserat. Sed ecquid est aliud? Rogandi igitur sunt Romani Correctores, ut & Augustodunensem istam ἀκυρολογίαν corrigere jam velint, & (si fatalis necessitas sic ferat, Error Errori Errorem ut semper pariat, atque Prodigium Dogmatis & nominis stribiligine æternum insigniatur,) ut ab altera porrò literula orsi, appellari hanc nunc jubeant, pro Transsubstantiatione, Vicesubstantiationem.
